title: Reviewer orientation: role, location search and a real write

steps.narration: Start at the storyboard's entry point.

title: Provisioning a new tenant, through the wizard's own validation

steps.narration: Open the platform's entry page.
Helena Voss, a platform Admin, opens the Super Admin console sign-in page.
She enters her work email.
...and a password — any non-empty value is accepted for an active account.
She signs in, landing on the platform dashboard, the console's home surface.
She opens the tenant list.
She clicks Create tenant.
She types the new tenant's name.
With the name valid, Next advances to Commercial.
She selects the Growth tier.
Commercial is valid by default; Next advances to First administrator.
She names the tenant's first administrator.
...and their email — the address the invitation goes to.
Both administrator fields are valid; Next advances to Review.
She opens the review confirmation.
She confirms the tenant and its administrator invitation.
Finish commits the tenant and its administrator invitation as one real write.
The write lands her on the new tenant's own detail page, Invited. Activate is present but disabled, and the reason is stated: no administrator has accepted the invitation yet.

action.description: The new tenant's Activate control renders disabled, with its reason stated.

title: A Tenant Admin accepts, and the platform team activates the workspace

steps.narration: Open the platform's entry page.

Before anything else, this run makes sure no session is carried in from an earlier tour — a fresh page load would guarantee that on its own, but a tour launched right after another must establish it for itself.
It tries an address this platform does not recognise.
...and a password.
The attempt is refused, and — like any unsuccessful sign-in — leaves no session behind.
Nadia Ferreira opens the invitation link Ironclad Fasteners' Tenant Admin was sent.
She accepts the invitation — a real write that activates her own account and lands her, signed in, on the Hub. Her workspace is visible but not yet operating.
She signs out from the Hub's own account menu.
Helena Voss, a platform Admin, opens the console sign-in page to activate the workspace now that its administrator has accepted.
She enters her work email.
...and a password.
She signs in.
She opens Ironclad Fasteners' own detail page.
With Nadia's acceptance now on record, Activate is enabled. She clicks it.
...and confirms — a real write moving the tenant from Invited to Active.
Back on the tenant list...
...searching for Ironclad Fasteners shows its row now carrying the Active status.

title: Building the Site, Area and Location hierarchy

steps.narration: Open the storyboard's entry point.
Dana Whitfield, the Tenant Admin, opens the console sign-in page — the one sign-in screen every surface in this build shares.
Dana Whitfield, the Tenant Admin, enters a work email — this session's own identity for every write that follows.
...and a password — any non-empty value is accepted for an active account.
Signs in, landing on the platform dashboard — the shared console home every role lands on first.
She opens Location Configuration — Sites, the top tier of the hierarchy.
She clicks Create site. Only the Tenant Admin can reach a live control here — a Supervisor or Quality Manager would see the same button disabled, with the reason stated.
She names the new Site.
...and its address.
...and a contact email.
She sets the Site's own timezone — Areas and Locations beneath it inherit this, with no override of their own.
Create site commits the write for real, through the same door a Supervisor's identical attempt would be refused at.
She opens an existing Site's Areas tier — Northgate Components Plant.
She clicks Create area.
She names the new Area, under Northgate.
Create area commits the write.
She opens an existing Area's Locations tier — Wheel Build, also at Northgate.
She clicks Create location.
She names the new Location.
...and the certification a Worker must hold to be assigned here — free text; the source names no closed set of certification types.
Create location commits the write — the third and final tier of the same hierarchy, all three Tenant-Admin-only.

title: The User, Device and Site legs of a tenant's slow decline

steps.narration: Open the storyboard's entry point.

Signs in, landing on the platform dashboard — the shared console home every role lands on first.
The User leg: she opens Diego Fuentes' own worker record.
She opens his Qualifications tab.

No control anywhere in this build lets a Tenant Admin manually suspend a tenant user's own account. The real, schema-carried analogue to a person 'lapsing' is a qualification's own expiry running its course, exactly as seeded here — observed, not enacted.

action.description: His Paint Booth Respirator Certification already renders Expired.

steps.narration: The Site leg: she opens Location Configuration's own Sites tier, home to Riverside Plant.

A Site's own closure is real here as Archive — the nearest genuine action to 'a Site closure' this build has. Riverside itself cannot close while its Areas are still active, so the attempt is refused and named, not silently blocked.

action.description: Archive renders, disabled, naming Riverside's own active Areas.

steps.narration: The Device leg: she opens Devices.
She searches the fleet for the specific device the platform has already de-authorised.

title: Watch a Supervisor's own worker-invite refused mid-flow

steps.narration: Open the storyboard's entry point.
Marco Ellis, a Supervisor, opens the console sign-in page.
He enters a work email — this session's own identity for every write that follows.
...and a password — any non-empty value is accepted for an active account.
Signs in, landing on the platform dashboard.
He opens Worker Lifecycle and Qualifications — the module's own write door reads him as an operational writer, so Add worker renders live, not disabled.
He clicks Add worker.
He chooses to invite a new worker — the first of its two real writes creates an account and grants it a role in one step.
He names the new account.
...and its email.

Create account and continue is refused — a live control on this screen is not the same as standing to complete the write behind it. Only a Tenant Admin may grant any tenant role, the Worker role included, and this door checks that fact for real, not merely the role floor to attempt it.
